newsitem.title: USA: D'Amato presses Clinton on Iran-Libya sanctions.
newsitem.headline: D'Amato presses Clinton on Iran-Libya sanctions.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Alfonse D'Amato stepped up calls Thursday for the Clinton administration to carry out sanctions against new investments in Iran and Libya, under a law signed two months ago.
"All that we have heard from your Administration regarding the enforcement of this law is that it is monitoring the situation," D'Amato said in an October 10 letter to President Bill Clinton.
The law calls for Washington to slap sanctions on anyone who invests $40 million or more in any one year in oil or gas projects in Iran or Libya.

Pointing to a $600 million agreement which Iran said it signed this week with a consortium of German and South Korean companies to build a petrochemical plant, D'Amato said "the deal should be sanctionable under the law."

"We can wait no longer," said D'Amato, who led the congressional effort to isolate Iran and Libya. "If one deal can be allowed to go through, then more will follow, negating any progress we have already made on this issue."

Administration officials have said they are crafting guidelines on how to enforce the law and are still collecting information on three other oil and gas agreements which Iran has signed since the beginning of August.
